chunks: My father (rah) said: Sa'd: It was narrated to me by Sa'd ibn Abdillah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Abdul-Adheem from Abdillah al-Alawi from al-Hasan ibn Ali from some of our companions from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
One who is needy and does not accept Zakat, is like one on whom Zakat has become obligatory and he is not paying it.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on refusing to accept Zakat if one is eligible?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to emphasize the gravity of neglecting Zakat by drawing a legal analogy: withholding obligatory Zakat is equated with refusing it when one is eligible to receive it. This highlights that the spiritual and legal consequences of omission are severe, regardless of whether the individual is the payer or the recipient, reinforcing the communal obligation of wealth purification in Shia jurisprudence.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Sa’d b. Abdillah from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from Abdul-Adheem from Abdillah al-Alawi from al-Hassan b. Ali from some of our companions from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
One who is needy and does not accept Zakat, is like one on whom Zakat has become obligatory and he is not paying it.”
